> 大道甚夷，而民好徑.

Chapter 52 was about closing the mouth and returning to the mother. Chapter 53 lifts the eyes and looks at the age.

Three characters carry the chapter, and all three are harsher in their original sense than in modern use.

## 徑 is a footpath one person wide

徑: 步道也 — a walking path, the kind only a person can use, not a cart.

So 民好徑 is not "people like shortcuts" as a mild complaint about laziness. A 徑 is a path that cannot carry a wagon, cannot hold two abreast, cannot be shared.

The narrowness is the accusation. What people prefer is not a faster road; it is a road that only one person can walk at a time.

## 大道甚夷

The great way is 夷 — level, flat, easy to walk.

夷 is also the name of the first of chapter 14's three invisibles: 視之不見，名曰夷. The connection is worth holding: the great way is easy because it is level, and it is invisible because there is nothing about it to catch the eye.

A road with no features offers no way to distinguish yourself on it.

## 盜 and 夸

盜: 私利物也 — to covet another's vessel, to want a thing that is not yours. Its original sense is the private desire for a particular object.

夸: 奢也, and the character is built from 大 and 亏 — to speak it large, until it runs to deficit.

So 盜夸 is not "a boasting robber." It is: taking what is public and calling it one's own, then inflating it. The inflation and the appropriation are the same act — the 亏 is built into the 大.

## 朝甚除，田甚蕪，倉甚虛

The court is 甚除 — thoroughly cleaned, swept, ornamented. The fields are 甚蕪 — overgrown. The granaries are 甚虛 — empty.

Three 甚's in a row, and the sequence is the argument: the level of finish at the top is in direct proportion to the dereliction below.

除 is the key verb — to clear, to clean, to prepare. The court's beauty is not an ornament added to the state; it is work taken from somewhere.

## 服文采，帶利劍，厭飲食，財貨有餘

Wearing patterned silk, carrying a sharp sword, satiated with food and drink, goods in surplus.

Note what is on the list. None of these are crimes. Each is a marker of a position that has been converted into a display.

厭 is to be full to repletion — the point where the appetite has been exhausted rather than satisfied.

## 是謂盜夸。非道也哉

> 是謂盜夸。非道也哉！

This is called 盜夸. This is not the way — 也哉!

The final exclamation is unusual: Laozi rarely raises his voice. And what he is exclaiming about is not cruelty or corruption in the ordinary sense. It is the aesthetic condition of a state whose surface has been finished while its base has been emptied.

## Why the narrow path

Put the two halves together and the chapter's logic appears.

The 大道 is level and shared. The 徑 is narrow and private. The court's finish is a private path: it can only be walked by those who have taken from the fields and granaries to build it.

And anyone on such a path is, structurally, alone on it.

## A test

Look at the surface of any organization you know and ask what has been swept, and what is overgrown underneath. The ratio is usually the chapter's diagnosis, and it is visible without any inside information.
